name: Freakwater
label: Thrill Jockey
lede: Two Kentucky singers recorded harmonies in a basement in 1985 and went on making honky-tonk for indie crowds for thirty years, through a long silence and a reissue that restarted them.

eras.title: Mojo Wishbean and Trippy Squashblossom
eras.text: Janet Beveridge Bean and Catherine Irwin recorded their first harmonies in a Kentucky basement in 1985 and put out a record in 1989. Bean was drumming in Chicago's Eleventh Dream Day at the same time, and Freakwater ran alongside it.

years.h: Two Kentucky singers find their harmony in a basement
years.p: Bloodshot Records dates Freakwater to 1985, when Janet Beveridge Bean and Catherine Irwin recorded their first harmonies in Bean's parents' basement.

years.big: "Establishing our early desire to do the wrong thing."
years.h: Mojo Wishbean and Trippy Squashblossom cover Woody Guthrie
years.p: Bean on the dulcimer-driven punk take on a [[Woody Guthrie|cbd827e1-4e38-427e-a436-642683433732]] song that she and Irwin cut for the 1987 WNUR compilation Hog Butcher to the World, under those names.
years.xp: WNUR is Northwestern University's radio station. Bloodshot's bio gives the pseudonyms and the quote, and reads the track as the duo's founding instinct.

years.h: Amoeba puts out the debut, as it had for Eleventh Dream Day
years.p: Freakwater's first album comes out on Amoeba Records, the same small label that issued Eleventh Dream Day's first records.
years.xp: Bloodshot's bio spells the title Freak Water and says the band's first live show was at a Louisville strip club that ran a punk open-mic night.

years.cap: Janet Bean, Dave Gay and Catherine Irwin after a soundcheck at the Cubby Bear, Chicago, 1989
years.src: Bloodshot Records: Freakwater · Thrill Jockey: Freakwater
years.h: Dave Gay, late of Stump the Host, picks up the bass for good
years.p: The debut LP leads Bean and Irwin to David Wayne Gay, formerly of Stump the Host. He has played bass in Freakwater ever since.
years.xp: Bloodshot's bio calls Gay "the steely heart of the band ever since." Thrill Jockey's band lineup lists him as bassist beside Irwin, Bean and pedal steel player Jon Spiegel.

years.h: Black Sabbath's War Pigs turns up on their first single
years.p: The 1 1/4 York Records release pairs Your Goddamned Mouth with Freakwater's cover of [[Black Sabbath|5182c1d9-c7d2-4dad-afa0-ccfeada921a8]]'s War Pigs.

years.h: Amoeba issues the second album, Dancing Under Water
years.p: The follow-up to the debut, again on Amoeba. Thrill Jockey reissued it in 1997.

eras.title: Honky-tonk for the indie kids
eras.text: Freakwater signed to Thrill Jockey, a young Chicago label, and made four albums there between 1993 and 1999. The Chicago Tribune heard loss and hardship told in gorgeous harmonies; Bean says the band's lack of ordinary ambition is what kept the loyal fans loyal.

years.h: Feels Like the Third Time is the first for Thrill Jockey
years.p: Out with City Slang in Europe, and a single that pairs My Old Drunk Friend with Kentucky.

years.h: Freakwater land on a Carter Family tribute
years.p: Amoeba's Keep on the Sunny Side: A Tribute to the Carter Family includes them. Critics had compared Bean and Irwin's harmonies to [[The Carter Family|29c5b1fb-5dcc-4499-b225-4ceeeb8a73d1]] from the start.

years.h: Freakwater show up in the road movie Half-Cocked
years.p: Wikipedia lists the band as appearing in Half-Cocked, a 1994 indie road movie.
Freakwater's third album, on Thrill Jockey and City Slang. A single paired South of Cincinnati with Cut Me Out.
years.xp:
Hilary Saunders wrote in Paste that "Old Paint musically looks backwards. It has the jauntiness of barn dances, complete with fiddles, dobros, and tambourines."

Her point about the singers: the two voices, content in their different ranges, tell country tales that still sound ahead of their time.

years.p: Out on LP and CD, the third of Freakwater's four Thrill Jockey albums in the '90s.
The album comes with a single pairing Hellbound and Lorraine.

eras.title: Solo detours, then Chicago
eras.text: After End Time Bean and Irwin each made a solo record for Thrill Jockey. Irwin then moved from Louisville to Chicago, and Freakwater came back with Califone in the room.

years.src: Thrill Jockey: Freakwater · Bloodshot Records: Freakwater
years.h: Catherine Irwin and Janet Bean make solo records
years.p: Irwin puts out Cut Yourself a Switch and Janet Beveridge Bean puts out Dragging Wonder Lake, both on Thrill Jockey. The label called them "natural marks on the Freakwater continuum."
years.xp: Thrill Jockey's bio describes Irwin's record as "achingly sincere" and Bean's as "lush, heartbreaking." Release years vary by source; Bloodshot dates both to 2002.

q: you can play it into your 80's; you just play it a little slower.
years.h: Irwin moves to Chicago, and Thinking of You follows
years.p: After six years off, Catherine Irwin leaves Louisville and Freakwater record with labelmates [[Califone|68025033-de1b-42f5-8a21-bedfb8895dda]], produced by [[Tim Rutili|8763bab7-fbfa-41ae-90d4-e5fdbb1ad63c]] at Clava Studios.
years.xp:
Califone's Joe Adamik, Ben Massarella and Jim Becker played on it, along with Jacob Smith and [[James Elkington|0b4020a0-0126-4574-bbed-d9109ed60b8a]], and Freakwater toured with Califone members that year. It was their last album for eleven years.

Irwin on the pull of it: "The sound of two voices singing at the same time is a beautiful thing - everything else is a chore."

eras.title: The reissue that restarted them
eras.text: A twentieth-anniversary reissue got Freakwater working again. Bean and Irwin toured the old record, moved to Chicago's Bloodshot Records, and sang about coal with two Mekons.

years.p: Janet Bean and Catherine Irwin start working as Freakwater again after a break that began in 2006, prompted by the reissue of Feels Like the Third Time.

years.h: Freakwater and two Mekons sing about coal
years.p: Bean and Irwin join [[Jon Langford|df3f656e-5083-40a1-8e51-d111b3d65992]] and [[Sally Timms|41397aa6-1f3e-4a95-b3a6-6649bdbdbf2a]] of the [[Mekons|66d2169c-dea5-46d3-b4cb-52ed87b24ab0]] as the Freakons, singing mining songs from Appalachia, England and Wales for Kentuckians for the Commonwealth.
years.xp: The Freakons played Hardly Strictly Bluegrass in San Francisco and the Hideout in Chicago in 2013, then again in September 2017 with violinists Jean Cook and Anna Krippenstapel, and in July 2021.

years.cap: Freakwater under a Country & Western Music sign
years.h: Freakwater take Feels Like the Third Time back on the road
years.p: The reissued album is the core of the 2014 shows.

years.cap: Freakwater at The Bell House, Brooklyn, February 16, 2016
yt: Take Me With You, live in Utrecht, 2016
years.h: Eleven years on, Scheherazade lands on Bloodshot
years.p: Freakwater's first full-length since 2005, preceded by a 2015 single pairing The Asp & the Albatross with Fullerene.
years.xp:
Bloodshot's bio puts the band's contrariness at the center: in Bean's words, their lack of normal ambition and their failure to capitalize on acclaim is what endeared them to their most loyal fans.

The Chicago Tribune said they "fill tales of loss and hardship with gorgeous harmonies and homespun warmth." No Depression heard an "intentional dissonance" owing as much to Sonic Youth as to Hazel & Alice.

years.h: A live Freakons album, from the Hideout in 2017
years.p: Fluff & Gravy releases it, recorded at the September 2017 Hideout shows by Bean and Irwin with Jon Langford and Sally Timms.
